rule: If you name it here, it must exist as a row on its own tab
why_it_matters: The workbook is a network, not a set of independent lists. A cell naming a system, owner, function or platform is a link to a row elsewhere. When that row is missing, we lose the connection between the two things while both still appear individually — which is what makes it hard to spot.
what_breaks_without_it: We received 'Emergency Department Operations' referenced by several rows but never listed on the business functions tab. Everything about it — who owns it, what systems it uses, what it costs — was dropped.
how_to_check_before_sending: Filter each reference column and confirm every distinct value appears on the tab it belongs to.

why_it_matters: We match by name. Two spellings become two things, or one of them matches nothing at all.
what_breaks_without_it: 'Epic Hyperspace' on one tab and 'Epic HyperSpace (Prod)' on another became two separate systems, splitting their cost, ownership and risk.
how_to_check_before_sending: Copy names from the tab that owns them rather than retyping. Sort each reference column and look for near-duplicates.

rule: A name column takes a name, never a description
why_it_matters: A reference column identifies a thing. A sentence about the thing identifies nothing, so the relationship cannot be recorded.
what_breaks_without_it: We received "Epic's SQL-Server-based operational reporting database" in a column expecting a platform name. It should have been 'Epic Clarity' — the description belongs in the notes column, where it is valuable and kept.
how_to_check_before_sending: If the cell contains a verb, it is probably a description.

rule: A category is not a thing
why_it_matters: Classifications describe how something is hosted or connected. They are useful and they belong in the hosting-model or integration-type column. In a reference column they name nothing.
what_breaks_without_it: 'Vendor SaaS', 'Direct point-to-point' and 'SQL Server (on-prem)' appeared where a specific platform was expected, so those relationships could not be recorded at all.
how_to_check_before_sending: If you could point at a screen or a contract and say 'that one', it is a thing. If it describes a whole class, it is a category.

rule: Pick one owner convention and hold to it
why_it_matters: This is the single largest source of unresolved references. It is a decision, not a data-collection exercise, and it should be made on day one.
what_breaks_without_it: 'CMO' in one column and 'Chief Medical Officer' in another are two different owners to us. Abbreviations are fine — as long as they are the only form used.
how_to_check_before_sending: List org units and their leaders on the organisation tab first, then reference those exact labels everywhere else.

rule: Separate multiple values with semicolons, not commas
why_it_matters: Names contain commas. 'Distribution, Sales & E-Commerce' is one function and we cannot reliably tell it from two.
what_breaks_without_it: Comma-separated data domain lists were split mid-name, producing fragments that matched nothing.

rule: If you reference by ID, define the ID once
why_it_matters: Referencing by ID is welcome and often better than by name. It only works if the ID appears in the ID column of the tab that owns the item.
what_breaks_without_it: Integration rows referenced applications as 'APP-0003' where the applications tab had no such ID populated, so none of them resolved.
how_to_check_before_sending: Reference by ID or by name, but do not mix the two for the same kind of thing across tabs.

rule: Leave it blank rather than filling it in
why_it_matters: A blank is honest and we report it as a gap you can decide to close. A placeholder looks like data, so we have to detect and discard it — which costs you a round trip.
what_breaks_without_it: 'TBD', 'N/A', 'various' and 'enterprise' were supplied in value columns and had to be stripped, with 1,708 placeholder values recorded as gaps.

rule: Where a number is an estimate, say so in the confidence column
why_it_matters: We will quote your numbers back to your executives. A figure marked high-confidence is treated as evidence; one marked estimated is labelled as directional. Both are useful — being unable to tell them apart is not.
what_breaks_without_it: Unmarked estimates get presented with the same weight as audited figures, and the first person to challenge one undermines the whole page.
how_to_check_before_sending: Use the confidence column on every row carrying a number you did not take from a system.

rule: For outcomes, tell us why you cannot claim it yet
why_it_matters: This is the only place we ask for a judgement rather than a fact, and it is the one that decides whether anything can be presented to a board. 'Missing actual' tells us a field is blank. 'The instrumentation was never funded' tells us who to call.
what_breaks_without_it: Without it, we infer the reason from which fields are empty — technically accurate and nearly useless. In one review that inference made 80 of 102 outcomes look claimable when the client would stand behind 16.
how_to_check_before_sending: Fill claim_readiness, claim_blocked_reason, unblock_action and unblock_target_period on the metrics tab.
